notes: §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR6 restricts a numeric edited string to symbol combinations where 'The allowable combinations are determined from the order of precedence of symbols and the editing rules', with 'The number of digit positions that can be represented in the PICTURE character-string must range from 1 to 18 inclusive' and at least one editing symbol. AnalyzeCharacterString makes a string with an editing symbol NumericEdited; ScreenPictureDigitCapacity and CheckDigitCapacity hold its digit positions to EditionInfo.MaxDigits (18 below 2002); PictureComposition.Precedence walks the chart and, since kb/Work PB5175, gives a fixed currency symbol only the leading role below 2002 (§1985:VI.5.9.5 GR6: 'The currency symbol must be the leftmost character position to be counted in the size of the item'), so the prior PARTIAL's hole (PIC 999$) is closed. Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, d, f): refused Z(18)9, Z(18)P, $(20), *(18).99 (COBOL0802), 999$, +999$, 999$CR, 9$99, $-99, SZZ9, XZ9 (COBOL1935), $ and B (COBOL1934), +9.9E+99 (COBOL0900); accepted and edited right $$$9 [ $12], +$999 [-$012], -$99 [-$05], $(19) and +(19) at 18 digits, $Z(17)9, ZZ9.99CR [  1.50CR], ***9.99DB, $$,$$$.99- [$1,234.56-], 9/99/99, Z(16)P, ZZ.ZZ of zero [     ]. Classes a and e do not reach a PICTURE rule. The witness refuses PIC Z(18)9 with COBOL0802. next.reason: 1985: numeric edited uses 'B', '/', 'P', 'V', 'Z', '0', '9', ',', '.', '*', '+', '-', 'CR', 'DB', cs; 'The number of digit positions ... must range from 1 to 18 inclusive'; at least one editing symbol. §2023:13.18.40.4 GR13 a) defines fixed-point numeric-edited by an equivalent symbol test, combinations per §2023:13.18.40.3 SR2, content per §2023:13.18.40.4 GR14, but §2023:13.18.40.3 SR14 allows 'from 1 through 31' digit positions for fixed-point numeric-edited items: 19 to 31 digit edited pictures refused in 1985 are accepted.
